summary: RACI answers who does what for each WBS task. WBS is the foundation: every level-3 work package has a unique wbs_code that threads through RACI (rows), RAID (wbs_links), and the status report. Column headers are engagement people/roles (from WBS owners and named stakeholders); rows are WBS tasks.
generation_rules: Root JSON: {"roles": [ /* people/role column headers */ ], "rows": [ /* one per WBS task */ ]}.
Each row object: wbs_code (string, required), activity (string), assignments (object mapping role name to R, A, C, or I).
Include one RACI row per level-3 WBS work package; wbs_code must exactly match the WBS.
Set activity to the WBS element title (optionally prefixed with the wbs_code for readability).
Column headers in roles must be people/roles from the brief and WBS — use the same strings as WBS owner values.
Every role in roles must appear as a key in each row's assignments.
Each row must have exactly one Accountable (A) assignment.
The WBS owner for each task must hold R (Responsible — holds the pen) or A (Accountable) in that row.
Use R for who performs the work; A for who owns delivery; C for parties consulted; I for parties informed.
Do not use generic academic labels (e.g. Student Team, AI Agent System) — use engagement role names.
